articles.title: Forward-deployed engineers are the AI industry’s latest talent obsession | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Executive search firm Christian & Timbers estimates that there are only about 2,000 engineers in the U.S. with the special cocktail of sector know-how, gravitas, and hands-on applied AI experience needed to consistently help enterprises see a return on their AI expenditures.
“Not 2,000 available,” reads the study, shared exclusively with TechCrunch. “2,000 total.”
As enterprises move from trying to access the best models to figuring out how to implement them into workflows that meaningfully improves their bottom line, it appears the forward-deployed engineer (FDE) — engineers who work within client organizations to build, implement and deploy software or AI models — is about to become among the most sought-after specialist in the AI industry.
Demand for FDEs is already rising rapidly, according to the C&T study, which projects demand for these specialists to surge by 2,100% by the end of the year.
The research draws on interviews with more than 250 C-suite hiring executives across 180 companies, a focused survey of 80 Fortune 500 executives, and interviews with more than 300 FDEs and applied AI engineers between January and June 2026.
At the start of the year, only 5% to 10% of companies were planning to hire FDEs, and mostly only for small pilots. By the end of the second quarter, however, that number jumped to 70%, with the largest consulting and services firms reporting a need to increase their FDE headcount by 10 times, building full teams of 20 to 100 employees.
“This is all happening at a speed I’ve never seen. Enterprises are hiring in the middle of summer,” Jeff Christian, founder of C&T told TechCrunch.
That kind of demand will outstrip supply, if C&T’s study is accurate. The report found that there are roughly 17,000 U.S. FDEs on the market today, a good chunk of whom are already employed by Palantir, which invented the concept of the FDE years ago. (Christian said some of his clients are even buying Palantir’s technology just so they can access the firm’s FDEs.)
Only a fraction of the FDEs out in the wild are apparently elite enough to deliver true ROI, which these days is measured as “multiple tens of millions of dollars of ROI impact,” according to Christian. That could manifest as revenue acceleration on the go-to-market side (lead generation) or “replacing FP&A or replacing 2,300 document processors in India,” Christian says.
As Chris Taylor, CEO of Ode with Anthropic (a new FDE-focused services firm), put it: “Many FDEs are well equipped to help you roll Claude Code out to your workforce. Very few are capable of building your flagship AI product feature.”
Now that token-maxxing has morphed into value-maxxing, and enterprises taking a harder look at their balance sheets, accounting for AI spending is becoming more important than ever.
“This fall, [Wall Street] is about to say, ‘Hey, we’ve given you two years to figure this out…and you haven’t. There’s no ROI. So we’re going to start punishing those that have spent hundreds of millions, maybe even billions on this, and aren’t generating ROI, and rewarding those that have’,” Christian said.
AI companies are under pressure, too, as they’ve already spent tens of billions to train and deploy their models. For frontier AI firms, reaching profitability will depend on whether they can inject their technology into as many enterprises as possible, though that task is now being threatened by cheaper, increasingly capable open-weight models from China.
That’s why firms like OpenAI and Anthropic have set up their own ventures — Ode with Anthropic and OpenAI’s Deployment Company — and staffed them with FDEs whose sole purpose is to go forth and spread their tech around the enterprise.
It’s not only top AI firms and large consultancies clamoring for FDEs, however. Enterprises from insurance and fintech to healthcare and gaming, are seeking out these specialists, Christian said.
Companies are hiring teams of FDEs instead of bringing them in from firms like Ode, or Deployment Co, seeking to keep knowledge of proprietary processes in-house and protect them from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic.
“Everybody’s concerned that if they give up their proprietary business processes, [the AI firms] can compete with them, which is true in many different areas,” Christian said. “So having this muscle internally is so important.”
Taylor said he’s starting to hear the phrase “internal forward-deployed engineers” more often, but his clients aren’t yet asking Ode to put together internal FDE teams for them.
While many an enterprising young engineer might think they have the industry expertise and AI chops to take advantage of what may turn out to be a talent war, Christian warns that the FDE may not always be in demand.
“Maybe in two years, everything’s automated, and agents are automating agents as opposed to humans automating agents,” Christian said. “That is something that could occur. Hopefully, it doesn’t, and we continue to need these people within companies.”
In the medium-term, he thinks the need for FDEs will shift from enterprise AI to physical AI as companies try to implement things like humanoid robots into their workflows. But within five or 10 years, he says it’s entirely possible that the role of FDE will “go away.”
That may be true for all knowledge work, if AI leaders and CEOs’ vehement predictions come true. While C&T focuses on recruiting for fast-growing industries and hasn’t seen a pullback yet, Christian says more general search firms have definitely experienced a slowdown in recruitment requests.
Everything to do with AI is growing and in demand, he says. For now.
“I think that there’s absolutely a time soon where we’re going to see an impact in our business,” Christian said.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 30, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (July 30, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, July 30, 2026.
Communities residing in conflict zones need inner healing even as hotels threaten to stop taking orders on Swiggy, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
Featured news
Why this humanitarian believes inner healing is key to building peace in conflict zones
Working across Lebanon, Syria, Israel/Palestine, Mozambique, Sudan, South Sudan, Chad, and Congo convinced humanitarian Lena Lieberknecht that peacebuilding needs an inner dimension. Through the Art of Living, she is bringing stress-relief programmes to people living and working in conflict zones.
Read more
Bengaluru hotels warn of Swiggy boycott from Aug 15 over payment dispute
The Bangalore Hotels Association has alleged that Swiggy was deducting advertisement and promotional charges without obtaining written or digital consent from hotel owners before launching CPC, CPA, or promoted advertisements.
Read more
Funding news
Arboreal Bioinnovations raises Rs 230 Cr in Series A round co-led by EAAA and Omnivore
Arboreal Bioinnovations, a speciality food and nutraceutical ingredients technology company, has raised Rs 230 crore in a Series A round of funding co-led by EAAA, the alternative assets management arm of Edelweiss, and Omnivore. The round also saw participation from existing investor Rainmatter by Zerodha.
Aham Housing Finance raises Rs 100 Cr from The Sanmar Group
Chennai-headquartered Aham Housing Finance has raised Rs 100 crore in a follow-on funding round led by industrial conglomerate The Sanmar Group. Aham Housing Finance will use the funds to strengthen its lending capacity and accelerate expansion across underserved housing markets. The company will also use the funds to deepen its presence in existing geographies, enter select new markets, and continue investing in technology, underwriting and risk-management capabilities to better serve self-employed and first-time homebuyers.
Sid’s Farm raises over Rs 81 Cr in pre-Series B round
Direct-to-consumer brand Sid’s Farm has raised a pre-Series B funding round of over Rs 81 crore. Major investors who led this round included Omnivore, NSFO, Dodla Dairy, Next Bharat Ventures, and LIO along with a consortium of other investors, said the company in a statement. Hyderabad-based Sid's Farm is a dairy and food brand committed to making safe food a norm in Indian homes and serves over 50,000 families across multiple cities.
SUIND raises Rs 20.5 Cr seed funding
Autonomous unmanned aerial systems startup SUIND has raised Rs 20.5 crore in a seed funding round led by Transition VC, with participation from IIMA Ventures. The company will use the capital to expand commercial deployment of its DGCA-certified Bumblebee agricultural spraying drone, accelerate development of its WASP aerial intelligence platform, and strengthen its autonomy technology and engineering capabilities.
SUIND's vision-first autonomy platform enables drones to navigate challenging environments with minimal human intervention, overcoming limitations of GPS-dependent systems. While Bumblebee has been commercially deployed in plantations, the company is now targeting infrastructure inspection, industrial monitoring, surveillance and security applications through WASP. SUIND plans to scale manufacturing and commercial deployment over the next two years.
Hair beauty and styling brand Truth and Hair secures Rs 5.4 Cr
Hair beauty and styling brand Truth and Hair has raised Rs 5.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. The company will use the capital to strengthen its brand positioning, develop new products, expand marketing initiatives and widen its distribution network.
Its product portfolio includes Root Touch-Up Hair Mascara, 3-in-1 Curly Styler and Flyaway Wand, designed to cater to straight, wavy and curly hair. Truth and Hair said it is creating a new category at the intersection of hair makeup, styling and scalp health instead of competing directly with conventional shampoo and conditioner brands. The startup aims to redefine hair care with specialised beauty and styling solutions.
Kroslo raises Rs 5 Cr seed funding
Cookware startup Kroslo has raised Rs 5 crore in a seed funding round from Prath Ventures, Indian Silicon Valley, Unacademy co-founder Roman Saini and other angel investors. Prath Ventures contributed Rs 3.12 crore in the round.
The company develops titanium enamel cast iron cookware under its Tironox range, which it claims is up to 50% lighter than conventional cast iron and resistant to rust. Kroslo says its products address health concerns associated with scratched non-stick cookware that can release microplastics and toxic fumes. The startup plans to expand its product portfolio and strengthen its position in the premium cookware segment as consumer demand for healthier kitchen products grows.
Virat Kohli increases stake in Vault Fitness
Cricketer Virat Kohli and his brother Vikas Kohli have become strategic investors in premium fitness chain Vault by Virat Kohli, formalising a collective 28% equity stake in the company. Founded in 2023 by Mukesh Gogia, the franchise-led fitness brand currently serves over 30,000 members and plans to expand to more than 50 operational clubs by the end of the year.
Vault Fitness has a presence across Tier I and Tier II cities including Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, and now plans to target Tier III markets. The company partners with global fitness equipment brands including Matrix, Torque USA, Precor and Hyperice to offer premium training and recovery facilities.
Other news
Flipkart launches pay later credit offering
Flipkart Group has partnered with PayU Finance to launch Flipkart Pay Later, a new embedded credit offering across Flipkart, Myntra and Flipkart Minutes. The service provides customers with three repayment options—Pay Later with up to 30 days credit, Pay in 3 instalments, and EMI plans ranging from three to 12 months for higher-value purchases. The offering is designed for both everyday shopping and larger purchases across categories such as electronics, appliances, fashion and furniture.
PayU Finance, the NBFC arm of PayU, will serve as the licensed lending partner, while Flipkart Finance will manage customer relationships and credit intelligence. Additional financial institution partnerships are planned as the platform expands.
PhonePe launches PulsePro enterprise intelligence platform
PhonePe has launched PulsePro, an enterprise intelligence platform that converts aggregated transaction data into hyperlocal, near real-time market insights. The platform is designed to help businesses make data-driven decisions on expansion, distribution strategy, site selection and category growth. PulsePro offers solutions covering category and growth intelligence, retail network intelligence and hyperlocal market analysis.
Powered by PhonePe's network of over 700 million registered users, more than 50 million merchants and coverage across 99% of India's postal codes, the platform provides insights across over 200 store categories and 100 market signals. PhonePe said PulsePro builds on the success of its open-data platform PhonePe Pulse while offering enterprise-grade intelligence for businesses and organisations.
TakeMe2Space's satellite battery cleared for commercial use
Space technology startup TakeMe2Space has announced that its PowerBank-50 satellite battery pack has been successfully space-qualified after completing its first mission aboard Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 launch vehicle. The battery powered Cosmoserve Space's experimental payload at an altitude of 450 kilometres during the Mission Aagaman flight launched from Sriharikota on July 18.
Weighing just 380 grams, the battery offers over 50 Wh of energy storage and includes onboard intelligence to manage battery health and withstand harsh space conditions. Designed for CubeSats and microsatellites, the PowerBank-50 can support missions lasting up to five years in low Earth orbit. The company plans to offer the battery for future commercial satellite missions.
InCred Financial posts 82% jump in Q1 profit
InCred Financial Services has reported an 82.3% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 172 crore for the first quarter of FY27, driven by strong loan growth, improved operating efficiency and healthy asset quality. The company's loan book expanded to Rs 14,809 crore, supported by steady demand across its five lending businesses. Gross non-performing assets improved to 2%, while net NPAs declined to 0.7%, reflecting disciplined underwriting backed by its AI-enabled technology platform.
The cost-to-income ratio also improved to 44.6% during the quarter. InCred said its risk-first approach and proprietary technology continue to support stable asset quality while enabling the company to scale its retail-focused lending operations.
Abyro Capital launches SpaceTech platform Beacon
Venture capital firm Abyro Capital has announced the launch of Beacon, a dedicated platform to identify, invest in, and accelerate early-stage spacetech startups. Scheduled to be launched on August 3 in partnership with T-Hub, the programme will provide selected startups with an initial investment of $500,000 along with access to follow-on funding, mentorship from industry veterans and global market opportunities.
Beacon aims to bridge the gap between breakthrough space technologies and institutional capital by combining funding with technical guidance and market validation. T-Hub will support participating startups through its innovation ecosystem. The initiative comes as India's private space sector witnesses growing investment and commercial opportunities following sector reforms.
Shiv Nadar AIC launches startup-investor platform
The Shiv Nadar Atal Incubation Centre, in partnership with StartinUP, has launched The Capital Connect, a startup-investor engagement platform aimed at improving access to funding and strategic partnerships. The inaugural event, held at HCL Group's Noida office, brought together over 50 startups, venture capital firms, alternative investment funds, corporates, government officials, and ecosystem leaders.
A key highlight was the Venture Connect segment, where 20 selected startups held one-on-one meetings with interested investors to discuss funding and business expansion. The organisers said the initiative will become a sustained platform to strengthen investment readiness, deepen founder-investor engagement, and accelerate the growth of technology-driven startups.
Amgen launches Scholars Programme in India
Amgen has launched the first Amgen Scholars Programme in India at the International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad (IIIT Hyderabad), supported through a two-year commitment until summer 2027. The inaugural cohort comprises 10 undergraduate students from India, Vietnam, Qatar and Dubai, who will undertake a two-month residential research programme focused on artificial intelligence, machine learning, drug discovery, genomics and healthcare.
Participants will work alongside IIIT Hyderabad faculty, attend seminars and networking sessions, and present their research through scientific posters. They will also participate in the regional Amgen Scholars Symposium in Tokyo. The programme aims to encourage scientific research and inspire future innovators while strengthening international collaboration in advanced sciences.
Hyperlocal discovery platform DashLoc marks four years, expands AI offerings
AI-powered hyperlocal discovery platform DashLoc has completed four years of operations, evolving from a bootstrapped startup into a global SaaS company serving businesses across 12 countries. The company currently works with over 250 brands and plans to expand its customer base to more than 400 brands as it strengthens its international presence.
DashLoc has also expanded its product portfolio with enterprise solutions including DashVoice for AI-driven customer interactions, DashDesk for automated customer support and DashORM for online reputation management.
The company said eight additional AI-powered products are under development as it continues to help businesses improve digital discoverability, customer engagement, and operational efficiency across multiple locations.
ValuePitch expands AI research partnership with SMVIT
ValuePitch has strengthened its partnership with Sir M Visvesvaraya Institute of Technology (SMVIT) by establishing the Centre for Advanced AI Innovation & Research to bridge the gap between academia and industry. The centre will focus on technologies including generative AI, agentic AI, computer vision, artificial intelligence, machine learning, decision intelligence, Data Analytics and Cybersecurity.
The collaboration builds on a relationship that began in 2018 and has already enabled internships for around 30-40 students while benefiting nearly 1,200 students through hackathons and innovation initiatives. The initiative aims to equip students with practical industry experience and enhance their employment opportunities in emerging AI technologies.
FinStackk targets 1,000 business customers
Accounting and tax compliance automation platform FinStackk has announced plans to support 1,000 businesses by the end of the current financial year after crossing the milestone of serving more than 500 companies. The platform helps Indian startups and businesses expanding into the United States manage incorporation, accounting, taxation, payroll, compliance and legal requirements through an integrated technology platform.
To strengthen its offerings, the company is investing in AI-powered products including Fin-Comply, Practice Management Solution, Sales Tax Platform and Fin-Stock, a cap table management solution. FinStackk said the new products will simplify compliance, automate financial workflows and improve operational visibility for growing businesses operating across international markets.
GlobalLogic recognised by Everest Group and ISG
GlobalLogic, a Hitachi Group company, has been recognised as a Leader and Star Performer by Everest Group while also retaining leadership across all categories in the ISG Provider Lens Digital Engineering Services study. Everest Group recognised the company in its 2026 Software Product Engineering Services PEAK Matrix for strong growth, expanding client base and improved market capabilities.
GlobalLogic also maintained its leadership position across all evaluated categories in ISG's Digital Engineering Services study for the US market, including augmented design and R&D services, intelligent operations, connected experiences, and integrated platform and application services. The company said the recognition reflects its continued focus on AI-first digital engineering and scalable innovation.
VECROS launches AI autonomy platform for drones
Deeptech startup VECROS has commercially launched Jetcore, an India-designed AI autonomy compute platform for drones and robotic systems operating in GPS-denied environments. The platform combines AI computing, real-time flight control, multi-sensor connectivity, embedded firmware and the company's proprietary Jetpix autonomy software into a single integrated system.
Jetcore enables advanced onboard AI capabilities including obstacle avoidance, visual-inertial odometry, SLAM, 3D mapping and autonomous mission execution without continuous cloud connectivity. Following more than 5,000 autonomous flight hours and early commercial validation, VECROS is making the platform available to drone and robotics manufacturers across defence, industrial inspection, warehousing, mining, utilities, agriculture, public safety and infrastructure monitoring sectors.
NTT DATA launches ADAPTIS payment solutions brand
NTT DATA Payment Services India has launched ADAPTIS, a unified brand bringing together its payment acceptance, merchant services and commerce solutions under one platform. Designed for neighbourhood merchants, MSMEs and large enterprises, ADAPTIS enables businesses to accept digital payments, manage commerce operations and deliver seamless customer experiences across online and offline channels.
The platform offers four service categories in India—ADAPTIS In-Store, e-Commerce, Enterprise and Value-Added Services. NTT DATA said the integrated platform will simplify payment management while improving operational efficiency and customer engagement. The company currently serves millions of merchants and processes over 100 million transactions annually through its PCI-DSS compliant payment infrastructure.
Snowflake unveils Cortex AI Gateway
Snowflake has introduced Cortex AI Gateway along with new AI security capabilities aimed at enabling secure deployment of enterprise AI agents. The platform provides organisations with centralised governance, visibility and cost control across both first-party and third-party AI agents. Cortex AI Gateway allows enterprises to manage access to AI models, applications, tools and enterprise systems while monitoring agent activity and optimising AI consumption costs.
Supporting more than 100 Model Context Protocol servers, the gateway also intelligently routes requests to enterprise-approved AI models based on quality, cost and performance. Snowflake said the offering addresses growing governance and security challenges as enterprises increasingly adopt agentic AI across business operations.
IndieSemiC partners Semtech for LoRa-enabled chip platform
Fabless semiconductor startup IndieSemiC has partnered with Semtech Corporation to integrate LoRa wireless technology into its next-generation Sabarmati-1 System-in-Package platform. The collaboration aims to develop what the companies describe as the world's first 64-bit LoRa-enabled System-in-Package based on the VEGA RISC-V architecture.
The platform will combine 64-bit processing with ultra-low-power, long-range wireless connectivity to support applications including smart cities, industrial automation, smart metering, agriculture, logistics, healthcare and asset tracking. By integrating Semtech's globally adopted LoRa technology with indigenous chip design capabilities, the partnership seeks to strengthen India's semiconductor ecosystem and address the growing demand for intelligent, connected Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

articles.title: Google Docs s’appuie désormais sur Gemini pour illustrer vos documents
articles.text:
Gemini arrive officiellement dans Google Docs. Google vient d’en faire officiellement l’annonce, expliquant que « vous pouvez désormais créer et modifier des images, des diagrammes et des infographies directement à côté de votre texte à l’aide de Gemini dans Google Docs ». L’intelligence artificielle de Google utilisera le contexte de vos documents pour produire des visuels pertinents avec les données affichées dans celui-ci.
Gemini va vous aider à illustrer vos documents
Concrètement, l’arrivée de Gemini au sein de Google Docs doit vous permettre de créer et de retravailler des éléments graphiques sans avoir à quitter l’interface de Google Workspace. En se basant sur le contexte des documents sur lesquels vous travaillez, Gemini sera, par exemple, en mesure de créer des diagrammes et des infographiques. Vous pourrez ainsi demander à l’IA de résumer visuellement votre texte, en générant schéma récapitulant tous les éléments cités dans votre document.
Vous pourrez également demander à Gemini, en utilisant un langage naturel, de modifier l’aspect de certaines illustrations (en rectifiant par exemple le ratio), ou d’harmoniser le style visuel d’une image afin que celle-ci s’intègre parfaitement avec le reste du document.
Google précise par ailleurs qu’il sera possible d’appliquer une même modification simultanément sur plusieurs visuels et dans différentes parties du document.
Un déploiement en cours dans Google Docs, mais uniquement pour les abonnés
La firme de Mountain View a indiqué avoir commencé à déployer Gemini dans Google Docs ce 28 juillet. L’arrivée de l’assistant IA dans la suite bureautique de Google se fera néanmoins de manière progressive et ne pourrait donc être accessible aux utilisateurs qu’au cours des deux prochaines semaines.
À noter également que l’accès à Gemini dans Google Docs est limité aux utilisateurs possédant un abonnement payant. Les utilisateurs en disposant d’un abonnement entreprise Business Standard / Plus, Entreprise Standard / Plus, d’une formule Education Plus, et les particuliers dotés d’un abonnement Google AI Pro et Ultra seront les seuls à pouvoir en profiter.

articles.title: El ayuntamiento de Cangas pagó 200.000 euros de rescate por un ciberataque. Ahora están investigando a uno de sus concejales
articles.text:
En mayo de 2023 el ayuntamiento de Cangas de Morrazo sufrió un ataque de ransomware. Los atacantes amenazaron con vender los datos en la dark web si no se pagaba el rescate en bitcoin. El ayuntamiento acabó pagando y ahora hay una investigación en marcha para determinar si hubo alguna irregularidad, lo que ha puesto a uno de sus concejales en el punto de mira.
Qué está pasando. Tal y como informan en ABC, la jueza de la Plaza 2 del Tribunal de Instancia de Cangas ha citado a Antón Iglesias, actual concejal de Urbanismo, Vivienda y Medio Ambiente, en calidad de investigado con respecto al pago del rescate en cuestión. Lo llamativo, señalan en el Faro de Vigo, es que en el momento de los hechos, Iglesias no era concejal y ni siquiera fue él quien firmó el contrato de urgencia para pagar el rescate y recuperar los datos. Lo hizo Araceli Gestido, que en aquel momento acababa de llegar a la alcaldía. De momento no ha sido citada a declarar, aunque se espera que la jueza acabe llamándola.
La gestión del ataque. Tras el ciberataque, el Concello contrató a la empresa EVELB Técnicas y Sistemas S.L. para que realizara un estudio forense de los sistemas afectados. En este primer contrato se pagaron 5.279 euros a la empresa, pero no obtuvieron resultados y semanas después volvieron a contratarlos para recuperar los datos secuestrados. Esto sí funcionó, pero no por vías técnicas sino que negoció directamente con los atacantes y les pagaron el rescate en bitcoin. El total de este segundo contrato ascendió a 197.847,17 euros.
De qué se les acusa. Hacia finales de 2024, la Fiscalía de Pontevedra remitió al juzgado el caso por indicios de prevaricación, malversación de fondos, daños informáticos y coacciones. Lo que se investiga no es tanto el pago del rescate en sí, sino la gestión de estos contratos, los cuales se hicieron sin concurso público. Además, ambos fueron adjudicados a la misma empresa que ya había fracasado en su primer intento. Ahora, tanto la administración como la empresa están en el punto de mira.
El BNG, partido que gobierna en Cangas, ha mostrado su apoyo a Antón Iglesias, de quien dicen goza de "toda su confianza" y destacan que el gobierno actuó "conforme a los procedimientos legalmente establecidos".
Así fue el ataque. El ciberataque se produjo en la madrugada del 18 de mayo de 2023. El ransomware en cuestión fue LockBit 3.0 y se coló en los ordenadores del ayuntamiento a través de un correo de phising que fue abierto por un funcionario. Cuando los empleados llegaron a la mañana siguiente, se encontraron con sus ordenadores bloqueados en una pantalla que contenía un mensaje en inglés en el que pedían el rescate.
El cifrado afectó a más de la mitad de los equipos, bloqueando departamentos como el de contabilidad e impidiendo el pago de las nóminas y facturas de proveedores.

articles.title: La série d'action française GIGN domine complètement Netflix un peu partout
articles.text:
C’est ce qu’on appelle une frappe chirurgicale. Disponible depuis peu dans le catalogue de la plateforme au N rouge, la série française GIGN s’est emparée du sommet des tendances en France, reléguant au second plan le reste de la concurrence.
Un raz-de-marée chiffré qui confirme l’appétit insatiable du public pour les histoires de forces spéciales, de secrets militaires et de tensions familiales. De quoi le placer dans le top action Netflix, clairement.
Quand l’élite de la gendarmerie fait parler la poudre avec GIGN sur Netflix
Créée par Sylvain Caron et Julien Leclercq (déjà à l’origine du film phénomène AKA et du sous-estimé La Terre et le Sang), la série en 6 épisodes de 50 minutes plonge directement le spectateur dans le quotidien sous haute pression de l’unité d’élite de la gendarmerie nationale.
L’histoire suit David, un officier chevronné sur le point de raccrocher le treillis pour quitter le terrain. Mais son départ tourne au cauchemar lorsqu’une attaque d’une violence sans précédent frappe le GIGN de plein fouet. Pris entre l’intégration d’une nouvelle recrue, des soupçons de trahison et une vendetta personnelle qui le force à affronter son propre passé, David se lance dans une traque désespérée où le moindre faux pas peut coûter des vies.
Au casting : on retrouve un Tomer Sisley impeccable et ténébreux dans le rôle principal, épaulé par des pointures du cinéma d’action et du drame français comme Guillaume Gouix, Tristan Zanchi, Thierry Neuvic et Grégori Derangère.
Pourquoi tout le monde ne parle que de ça ?
Si GIGN domine le Top Netflix de la sorte, ce n’est pas un hasard. La série coche toutes les cases du grand divertissement d’action moderne :
- Un réalisme viscéral : armement (à quelques exceptions tout de même), tactiques de progression, gestion du stress… la patte de Julien Leclercq offre des séquences de fusillade et d’assaut à couper le souffle, d’une crédibilité irréprochable.
- Un drame humain fort : loin d’être un simple pan-pan décérébré, la série s’articule autour de liens familiaux brisés, du deuil, de la transmission et de la culpabilité.
- Un rythme sans temps mort : entre conspirations au sommet, missions solos d’infiltration et prise d’otages sous haute tension lors d’un final explosif, les six épisodes se dévorent en un seul week-end de binge-watching.
En remettant le savoir-faire de l’action « à la française » au centre du jeu, GIGN s’impose déjà comme l’un des plus gros succès tricolores de l’année sur la plateforme. Si vous ne l’avez pas encore dévorée, les 6 épisodes de la saison 1 sont actuellement disponibles en intégralité sur Netflix.

articles.title: Les contenus générés par IA devront bientôt afficher la couleur en Europe
articles.text:
À partir du 2 août, l’Union européenne fixe deux nouvelles obligations aux fournisseurs et utilisateurs de systèmes d’intelligence artificielle. Les contenus générés par IA devront porter un marquage visible ou technique et les chatbots devront signaler qu’ils ne sont pas humains.
La Commission européenne vient de préciser comment vous serez prévenus de contenus générés par des chatbots et par ordinateur. Elle confirme, par un règlement publié au Journal officiel le 24 juillet dernier, les obligations de l’article 50 de l’AI Act pour le 2 août.
En pratique, si un service client vous répond par un agent conversationnel, une mention devra l’indiquer, sauf évidence totale. Une photo, un son ou un texte informatif fabriqués ou fortement retouchés par IA, et publiés sans relecture humaine, devront eux aussi porter un signe reconnaissable, filigrane numérique ou mention visible. Les outils déjà commercialisés avant le 2 août bénéficient d’un sursis jusqu’au 2 décembre pour s’adapter.
Chatbots et contenus truqués devront afficher leur origine artificielle
Avec le Digital Omnibus, publié au Journal officiel le 24 juillet, la Commission conserve la même substance que le texte initial de l'AI Act sur ce point. Un agent conversationnel devra prévenir son interlocuteur humain dès le début de l'échange, sauf lorsque la nature artificielle de la conversation ne fait aucun doute pour un utilisateur normalement attentif. Une image, une vidéo ou un enregistrement sonore fabriqué par IA, ou fortement retouché, devra porter un marquage technique lisible par une machine. Le fournisseur ajoute une mention visible lorsque le contenu relève de l'information publique et n'a fait l'objet d'aucun contrôle éditorial humain.
Plusieurs plateformes ont anticipé cette échéance avant même son entrée en application. Google a par ailleurs rejoint le code de bonnes pratiques sur la transparence des contenus IA. La Commission et le comité européen de l’intelligence artificielle le jugent suffisant pour prouver sa conformité. YouTube a déplacé ses labels IA vers des zones plus visibles de son interface et ajouté une détection automatique pour les créateurs. Instagram teste de son côté un badge AI Creator, en complément de l’étiquette AI Info déjà proposée. Deezer et TIDAL ont annoncé, pour leur part, un étiquetage équivalent pour la musique générée par IA. Aux États-Unis, la décision revient aux entreprises elles-mêmes, faute de réglementation équivalente.
Les sanctions se chiffrent à 3 % du chiffre d’affaires, mais l’office IA manque d’effectifs
À partir du 2 août, la Commission européenne obtient des pouvoirs de sanction contre les fournisseurs de grands modèles, comme OpenAI. Elle peut réclamer des informations complémentaires ou exiger des changements techniques. En dernier recours, elle inflige une amende représentant jusqu’à 3 % du chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial de l’entreprise concernée.
L'’organe chargé de mettre en œuvre ces pouvoirs, l’Office IA de la Commission, compte 145 agents. Moins d’un quart d’entre eux travaillent directement sur la réglementation et le contrôle de conformité, selon Euractiv. Au moment de la négociation du texte, les risques systémiques liés à l’IA, comme les cyberattaques automatisées, étaient hypothétiques. Depuis Mythos d’Anthropic, c’est tout autre chose.
Mais outre-Atlantique, l’administration Trump fait barrage. Elle conteste les sanctions contre les entreprises américaines, selon lui, un facteur qui pourrait influencer la fermeté des autorités européennes. Brando Benifei, coauteur du règlement au Parlement européen, appelle malgré tout Bruxelles à défendre son texte avec fermeté.

articles.title: Il a suffi de 2 réglages simples à GPT pour faire beaucoup mieux que Claude
articles.text:
Tout part d’un tweet de victoire. Anthropic annonce sur son compte officiel que sur ARC-AGI-3, le score de son Claude Opus 5 est trois fois supérieur à celui du deuxième meilleur modèle, GPT-5.6 Sol. Un point donne du poids au chiffre : il a été mesuré par un tiers, la fondation ARC Prize, et non par Anthropic. Le résultat, 30,2 %, est un record sur ce test.
ARC-AGI-3, c’est quoi ? Un test pensé pour mesurer le raisonnement. On lâche le modèle dans de petits jeux en 2D qu’il n’a jamais vus, sans règle ni notice, et il doit comprendre seul comment ça tourne. Impossible, donc, de tricher en récitant des exemples avalés pendant l’entraînement.
Opus 5 y a bouclé cinq environnements qu’aucun modèle n’avait résolus, quand le GPT-5.6 Sol d’OpenAI plafonnait autour de 8 %. Ce genre de vérification indépendante reste rare : la plupart des scores brandis lors d’un lancement sont produits par le labo lui-même, sur son propre matériel. D’où le tweet triomphal.
Deux réglages, et l’écart s’effondre
Sauf qu’OpenAI n’a pas goûté la comparaison. Le 29 juillet, l’entreprise a publié une analyse au titre limpide : deux réglages ont triplé son score. Le test officiel s’appuie sur un « harnais » générique (la tuyauterie qui relie le modèle au jeu), et ce harnais jette le raisonnement du modèle après chaque action.
GPT-5.6 devait donc tout recomprendre à chaque tour, comme s’il perdait la mémoire en boucle. En activant deux options qu’OpenAI emploie déjà dans ChatGPT et Codex, la conservation du raisonnement et la compaction, le même modèle grimpe de 13,3 % à 38,3 %, avec six fois moins de jetons consommés. Soit, sur le papier, mieux que les 30,2 % d’Opus 5.
Le développeur autrichien Peter Steinberger (le papa d’OpenClaw), passé ingénieur chez OpenAI début 2026, a enfoncé le clou, se demandant tout haut si personne, chez Anthropic, ne s’était étonné de chiffres aussi absurdes avant de crier victoire.
La partie n’est évidemment pas neutre. ARC Prize, de son côté, reconnaît que le résultat d’OpenAI est réel et utile, tout en défendant son harnais volontairement basique : il impose à tous les modèles les mêmes conditions, pour comparer sur un pied d’égalité. Les deux labos, eux, se livrent déjà une guerre des agents de bureau autrement plus lucrative.
Au-delà de la bagarre d’egos, il y a une vraie leçon. Un benchmark ne mesure jamais un modèle tout seul : il mesure aussi le harnais, les réglages d’API et le niveau d’effort choisis par celui qui fait passer le test.
Le score d’Opus 5 tient la route parce qu’un tiers l’a vérifié. Celui de GPT-5.6 rappelle qu’un même modèle peut passer du simple au triple selon la plomberie autour. Avant de gober un « x3 » en gras, mieux vaut se demander qui a mesuré, sur quel harnais et à quel niveau d’effort.
D’ailleurs, Composio a récemment fait un test : faire tourner le modèle Kimi K3 sur trois harnais différents : Kimi Code, Hermes et Claude Code sur la même tâche. Le résultat est quasi similaire (la tâche a été effectuée), mais la consommation de tokens (et donc le coût) est radicalement différent. Une autre preuve que le harnais a presque autant d’importance que le choix du modèle.

articles.title: Ver la Conmebol Sudamericana en Fútbol Libre o Tarjeta Roja no es gratis: roban tus datos
articles.text:
Esta semana, los partidos de la Conmebol Sudamericana concentran la atención de millones de aficionados en toda la región, pero junto al interés deportivo surge una tendencia preocupante: muchos optan por acceder a las transmisiones a través de aplicaciones y sitios piratas como Fútbol Libre o Tarjeta Roja, sin conocer sus riesgos.
Según expertos en ciberseguridad, el acceso a plataformas no oficiales representa mucho más que una simple infracción de derechos de transmisión. Utilizar estos servicios puede exponer la información personal de los usuarios a amenazas informáticas, comprometer la seguridad de los dispositivos y acarrear consecuencias legales.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué peligros presentan las apps piratas para ver partidos
De acuerdo con ESET, las aplicaciones streaming piratas suelen estar ausentes de tiendas confiables como Google Play Store o App Store.
Esto obliga a los usuarios a buscar alternativas en sitios web poco confiables, donde no existen los filtros de seguridad y calidad que sí aplican las plataformas oficiales. Esta falta de control convierte a estas apps en un canal frecuente para la propagación de software malicioso.
PUBLICIDAD
Los riesgos van más allá de la simple visualización de contenido no autorizado. Estas aplicaciones tienden a solicitar permisos especiales y críticos en el dispositivo, abriendo la puerta a la instalación de malware, spyware y troyanos.
Según el reporte de ESET, “estas plataformas pueden convertirse en la puerta de entrada para el robo de información personal, la vigilancia remota o el secuestro de dispositivos”. El impacto puede extenderse a la red doméstica completa, afectando a otros dispositivos conectados.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo pueden robar datos personales a través de apps piratas
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad de España (INCIBE) explica que muchas de estas aplicaciones piden permisos que exceden los necesarios para su funcionamiento.
Una aplicación diseñada para ver gratis partidos puede solicitar acceso a la cámara, contactos, ubicación o incluso mensajes, sin justificación técnica. Cuando el usuario concede estos permisos, expone información sensible que puede ser utilizada con fines fraudulentos.
PUBLICIDAD
La recopilación de datos suele realizarse sin el conocimiento ni el consentimiento del usuario. Al instalar apps fuera de las tiendas oficiales, se pierde la protección que ofrecen los filtros de seguridad preexistentes.
Según INCIBE, “es fundamental revisar los permisos que solicita cualquier aplicación y desconfiar si piden acceso a funciones no relacionadas con el servicio”.
Qué riesgos legales puede tener el uso de sitios como Fútbol Libre o Tarjeta Roja
ESET advierte sobre los riesgos legales. Retransmitir contenidos sin contar con los derechos correspondientes constituye una violación de la propiedad intelectual.
En muchos países, los proveedores de internet pueden bloquear el acceso a estas plataformas por orden judicial, y los usuarios podrían enfrentarse a acciones legales si se demuestra que han distribuido o reproducido contenido protegido.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, el uso de estos servicios puede derivar en sanciones administrativas o penales, dependiendo de la legislación vigente en cada jurisdicción. Las plataformas que difunden partidos sin autorización suelen ser objeto de investigaciones y bloqueos constantes.
Cómo identificar una aplicación peligrosa antes de instalarla en el dispositivo
El INCIBE sugiere adoptar medidas preventivas para evitar la instalación de apps maliciosas. La primera pauta es descargar exclusivamente desde tiendas oficiales como Google Play Store o App Store, donde existen controles de seguridad y filtros para detectar software dañino.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra medida es leer las opiniones y valoraciones de otros usuarios antes de instalar una aplicación. Las reseñas pueden ofrecer pistas sobre problemas de seguridad, fallos recurrentes o comportamientos extraños de la app.
Qué hacer para proteger los dispositivos y los datos
Para mitigar las amenazas, tanto ESET como el INCIBE sugieren implementar varias estrategias. Mantener el sistema operativo y las aplicaciones actualizadas es una de las mejores formas de protegerse, porque las actualizaciones suelen corregir vulnerabilidades y mejorar la seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, realizar copias de seguridad periódicas de los datos personales permite recuperar la información si el dispositivo se ve comprometido. Estas medidas, combinadas, reducen la probabilidad de sufrir un ataque o una pérdida de datos.

articles.title: Knowledge graph architecture for enterprise AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Knowledge graph architecture gives enterprises ownership of the AI intelligence they create
Knowledge graph architecture has emerged from the concept stage, consigned to the realm of academia, to the production infrastructure stage, and the enterprises that shape it the right way will own the intelligence their AI creates.
That’s the central premise Shan Rizvi (pictured), founder and context architect at Thumos Care, is offering to practitioners who still treat AI retrieval as a search issue. Retrieval-augmented generation finds chunks of text, but it doesn’t reason, trace decisions back to evidence or accumulate knowledge over time. The rift between organizations that understand this and those that don’t will become one of the defining competitive divides of the agentic era, Rizvi noted.
“When you make an argument, there’s a premise, some reasoning applied to the premise, and then a conclusion,” Rizvi said. “Structure is quite inherent to thinking, and graphs, with the right ontology, are the obvious substrate.”
Rizvi spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier for an exclusive AI Luminaries interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why knowledge graph architecture is becoming the essential intelligence layer for enterprise AI, how to architect it across structured and unstructured data sources and what success actually looks like for teams trying to build a durable company brain. (* Disclosure below.)
Knowledge graph architecture enables traceable reasoning that enterprises own and control
The practical case for knowledge graph over search boils down to traversal. Rizvi described a startup building AI for truck parts maintenance. A system that needed to find all substitutes for a given part manufactured by companies meeting multiple criteria simultaneously. Search struggles with this kind of relational path-following at scale throughout millions of SKUs. A knowledge graph deals with it natively and can repeat the traversal recursively throughout different paths until the best answer materializes. This mirrors how human reasoning occurs, rather than how information retrieval has historically been engineered.
“That type of traversal is quite critical to reasoning,” Rizvi said. “Recursion is another key component. You might need to traverse certain paths in the graph, then repeat that traversal in different directions to find the best piece of information.”
For production deployment, the number one consideration is latency, Rizvi noted. Building a medical knowledge graph for Thumos Care using Neo4j — connecting diseases, symptoms, drugs and clinical guidance at scale — revealed that not all graph database platforms handle millions of nodes reliably. Recursive reasoning should only engage when necessary, with faster single-hop retrieval handling simpler queries to keep response times viable in production.
“Scalability is quite critical to consider,” Rizvi said. “If you’re dealing with millions of parts and tens of millions of SKUs, you need a graph database platform that can handle that reliably at a reasonable latency.”
On the question of data infrastructure, Rizvi drew a clear line between what belongs in a graph and what doesn’t. Structured, traditional databases with frequently changing data should remain in their native systems, with only their ontological structure represented in the graph so agents know what to query and when. Unstructured sources like Slack threads, meeting transcripts and chat logs are better candidates for direct extraction and ingestion into the graph, where their contextual meaning can be preserved and linked to domain entities over time.
“If you want to own a piece of the intelligence ecosystem, the piece you own has to be seen as intelligence, not as data,” Rizvi said. “You need an ontology for your domain, for knowledge, for cognition and for decision-making, and as long as you have those components, your models will get better as they’re used more frequently, and you will own that value.”

Os celulares da Oppo são focados em design premium e câmeras (a linha Find X tem parceria com a Hasselblad), além de serem pioneiros em carregamento rápido. A interface (ColorOS) também costuma ser vista como mais fluida e polida.

articles.title: GrapheneOS says its data-wiping "duress" password is perfectly legal, after user faces federal charges
articles.text:
Get Off My Phone: The recently unveiled case brought by the US Department of Justice against a GrapheneOS user is rekindling debate around privacy and effective operational security on mobile devices. The GrapheneOS Foundation has joined that debate, reaffirming some key points about the operating system's security features and whether previously deleted data can ever be recovered.
According to the GrapheneOS Foundation, the operating system that got Sam Tunick prosecuted by the US government has nothing to do with unlawful practices. The Toronto, Canada-based non-profit joined the fray to defend its open-source OS, which it maintains is a completely legal platform under US law.
The foundation says it has no obligation to weaken GrapheneOS features designed to improve user and data security. The Android-based OS, it argues, is protected by the US Constitution, meaning no one can (theoretically) be prosecuted for creating, developing, or even using the platform on their devices.
– GrapheneOS (@GrapheneOS) July 27, 2026
The foundation also believes any new law designed to make the software or its security features illegal would likely be unconstitutional. Similarly, the organization confirmed that once data has been wiped from a GrapheneOS-powered phone, there's no way to recover any of it.
The software, and the hardware it's compatible with (Google Pixel phones for now) is designed specifically to prevent attempts to bypass or tamper with data encryption.
Tunick ran into trouble after providing a US Customs and Border Protection officer with a "duress password," one of GrapheneOS' options for strengthening a user's right to privacy. Once used to forcibly unlock a phone, the duress password/PIN wipes all data on the device, including eSIM content. The process happens instantly, can't be stopped, and is irreversible.
The GrapheneOS Foundation has since tried to downplay the importance of duress passwords for the platform's security. The feature, the organization said, is just a minor option within a much broader security model. It can also carry physical or legal consequences, which is why users should carefully weigh whether it's the right approach for outsmarting attackers or coercive enforcement attempts by federal agents.
The lawyer representing Tunick against the US government said the border agent failed to read Tunick his Miranda rights, as required, and ignored his requests to speak with a lawyer. The lawyer is now trying to get a US judge to dismiss all evidence recovered in the case, arguing that Tunick's constitutional rights were violated.

articles.title: Russian $50m Su-57 crash sparks extraordinary Ukrainian claim
articles.text:
Ukrainian hackers claim to have shot down a $50m SU-57 fighter using Russia's own air defense
Russian air defense system strikes its own $50m fighter jet
- Ukraine says Russian defenses mistakenly destroyed one of Moscow's premier fighter jets
- InformNapalm claims cyber intelligence turned Russian air defenses against their own aircraft
- Russia insists a technical failure caused the reported Su-57 crash near Moscow
A Russian Su-57 fighter jet recently crashed in the Moscow region, and Ukrainian intelligence sources say it was no accident.
The international intelligence community InformNapalm claims a combined human and cyber intelligence operation manipulated a Russian air defense unit into striking its own aircraft.
The jet, valued at roughly $50 million, represents one of Russia's most advanced fighter platforms currently in active service.
How the operation reportedly unfolded
InformNapalm says the effort began earlier, when analysts processed a large volume of intercepted Russian communications and footage from a training ground.
That footage showed the BARS Moscow air defense system being trained specifically to counter Ukrainian long-range drones over the capital region.
Analysts used the material to build a detailed report covering personnel training, hardware, software, and combat algorithms tied to the system.
The report also identified specific vulnerabilities within the BARS Moscow network that outside actors could exploit.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This information was reportedly submitted to the Ukrainian Defense Forces, which allegedly used the findings during the operation.
“We thank our friends — cyber specialists of the future Cyber Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine,” InformNapalm emphasized, saying the intelligence gathered went beyond passive observation, and was instead used to influence how the specific air defense unit actually operated.
The group says this approach allowed the very system built by Russian engineers to be turned against a Russian aircraft.
The result, according to InformNapalm, was the destruction of the Su-57 by its own side's defenses, a claim that Russia vehemently denies.
Russia insists a technical failure caused the crash
The Russian Ministry of Defense attributed the crash to a technical malfunction, which is common rather than any external interference or sabotage.
InformNapalm disputes that account, noting reports of sabotage within the BARS Moscow system had already circulated in pro-Russian online spaces beforehand.
The group also points to a prior operation from 2025, called OKBMLeaks, in which it published documents from a Russian manufacturer supplying components for the aircraft.
That earlier material was translated into 13 languages and picked up by numerous international outlets covering the war.
However, there is no independent verification of InformNapalm's claim, leaving Ukraine's account directly contested by Russia.
Coincidentally, Russia's civil aviation authority Rosaviatsiya lowered the maximum flight altitudes near Moscow airports and banned transit flights over the region.
Officials cited security concerns tied to a rise in Ukrainian drone activity as the reason behind these restrictions.
Whether the security concern includes the recent case cited by InformNapalm remains to be seen.
Airlines remain worried that the changes could add 20 to 30 minutes to routes that once passed directly through Moscow's airspace corridor.
Kommersant, a major Russian business newspaper, also reported that the lower altitude ceiling raises the risk of bird strikes.
Whether the crash resulted from sabotage or a genuine technical fault, the competing accounts remain unresolved for now.

articles.title: I bought a power bank for summer travel, but it actually fixed my bedside cable nightmare
articles.text:
I bought a power bank for summer travel, but it actually fixed my bedside cable nightmare
With a TSA-friendly 25,000mAh shell and 170W output, EcoFlow’s Rapid Power Bank goes everywhere with me, from my nightstand to airport security
I bought the EcoFlow Rapid strictly for travel over the summer, but it ended up living on my nightstand. The outlet in my bedroom is blocked by the headboard, so keeping this battery on the table makes it way easier to charge my iPad while reading in bed. Nothing fancy, but it solved a daily annoyance right out of the box.
It's a fantastic way to beat charging woes even at full price - as I detail below. But US and UK readers can grab it for up to half-price, with the EcoFlow Rapid Power Bank down to $60 (was $130) at Amazon, while in the UK, the Rapid is now £65 (was £100).
At 25,000mAh (roughly 90 watt-hours), it sits right under the 100Wh limit TSA and most airlines set for carry-ons. Output maxes out at 170W total across two 140W USB-C ports and a 33W USB-A port—plenty of overhead to fast-charge a laptop and phone simultaneously without throttling either.
Recharging is equally quick: feeding it 140W gets the battery to 50% in about 20 minutes, which takes the stress out of low-battery warnings before a flight. There's a small color TFT display on the front that shows battery percentage and what's flowing through each port, so you're not guessing whether it's actually charging or just warm.
EcoFlow also includes in the usual protections you'd want in something you're tossing in a bag next to your laptop: overcharge, overheat, and short-circuit protection, along with a fire-resistant housing.
I found this power bank the best way to solve my charging problems thanks to the three ports that let me fast-charge my laptop and iPad.
In the UK: now £65 (was £100)
Where it actually earns its keep
Bedside, mostly. I like having my iPad plugged in while I half-watch something before I drift off, and I was sick of the nightly math: is there an outlet on this side of the bed, and is the cable even going to reach? Now the bank just lives on the nightstand and takes care of both problems at once.
Vacations are the other place it's become non-negotiable. On a trip, this thing is doing the work of what used to be three separate chargers: phone, tablet, and whatever camera or laptop
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
I've brought along, and because it clears TSA's carry-on limit, I've never had it questioned at security. Hotel rooms are notorious for having exactly one usable outlet near the bed, usually behind a nightstand you can't move, and having a full day of charging sitting in reach solves that without rearranging furniture.
Conferences are a battery killer. At a trade show a few months ago, my phone hit 20% before noon just from taking photos and answering Slack messages. The only nearby outlet had four different cables running out of it across the floor. I stopped hunting for plugs after that. Now I just charge my phone between talks and run a cable out of my bag to my laptop when it gets low.
It's also a solid answer for anywhere a plug isn’t guaranteed: a long flight, a road trip, a power outage at home, or a coffee shop where every outlet is already taken. That's really the point of a bank this size; it's not built for one scenario, it's built for the gap between wherever you are and the nearest working outlet.
A few things worth knowing before you buy
At just over a pound and roughly the size of a large candy bar, it's not the smallest power bank on the market, and that's a deliberate tradeoff for the output it delivers. If you only ever need to top off a phone, something smaller and lighter will do the job with less bulk in your bag. It also doesn't do wireless charging; everything works through the USB-C or USB-A ports, so you'll need a cable regardless of what you're charging.
One more thing worth noting: that 170W is a shared pool, not per-port. Plug in a laptop, a phone, and a set of earbuds at the same time, and the bank splits that 170W across all three rather than giving each one its own full rating. I've never actually perceived a slowdown using it that way, but don't expect three devices each pulling 140W simultaneously; that math just doesn't work.
For what it's actually meant to do- keep me charged through a flight, a conference floor, or just a lazy night in bed with the iPad- it's been reliable enough that I stopped thinking about battery anxiety altogether. That's a low bar to clear on paper, but it's exactly what made me trust it enough to bring it everywhere.
For more top picks, see our guide to the best power banks we've tested.
Bryan M. Wolfe is a staff writer at TechRadar, iMore, and wherever Future can use him. Though his passion is Apple-based products, he doesn't have a problem using Windows and Android. Bryan's a single father of a 15-year-old daughter and a puppy, Isabelle. Thanks for reading!

articles.title: Comcast store punished low sales by smashing pies in workers' faces, lawsuit claims
articles.text:
A lawsuit against Comcast’s cable division alleges that a store manager humiliated the lowest performing salesperson each month with a strange ritual in which a cream pie was smashed into the employee’s face. The lawsuit claims the store manager took videos of the assaults and ordered employees to participate in the assaults and record their own videos.
A Comcast store in Plainville, Connecticut, “had a policy that the highest-ranked Retail Sales Consultant for the prior month was instructed by his or her supervisor—Ms. Peterson, the Comcast Store manager—to tie the lowest-ranked sales consultant for the prior month to a chair in the back office and thereafter assault that person by violently smashing a cream pie in their face,” the complaint alleged.
Plaintiff David Figueroa’s lawsuit said he was hired as a retail sales consultant on February 2, 2026, and was supervised by store manager Sully Fuentes Peterson. Figueroa alleges that Peterson “designed and implemented” the pie-in-face ritual to meet goals related to sales and positive responses in customer surveys.
“Defendant did not inform the Plaintiff prior to his acceptance of Defendant’s offer of employment that the Comcast Store has a policy of subjecting Retail Sales Consultants to public assaults by co-workers—at the direction of Ms. Peterson, the store manager—for the purpose of increasing Defendant’s sales and profitability,” the lawsuit said.
Comcast was negligent, lawsuit alleges
Figueroa resigned on February 27, and he alleges it was a constructive discharge. The lawsuit says the defendant, Comcast, was negligent because it “reasonably should have known” about the store management’s policies and that the policies could harm employees. Comcast “failed to properly supervise the Comcast Store’s management team,” allowing store management to humiliate employees “for the purpose of promoting the Defendant’s revenues and profits,” the lawsuit alleged.

articles.title: Microsoft confirma una súper app de Copilot, y llegará muy pronto
articles.text:
Microsoft no se rinde con Copilot y ha confirmado que muy pronto va a lanzar una súper app basada en su IA. La idea de los de Redmond es agrupar todas sus herramientas de inteligencia artificial bajo un mismo techo, con el fin de darle nuevo impulso y simplificar su estrategia.
Si bien Microsoft todavía no comentó públicamente sobre los detalles finos de la súper app de Copilot, fue Satya Nadella, el CEO de la compañía, quien reveló que llegará en el corto plazo. Durante la presentación de resultados financieros del último trimestre, el ejecutivo remarcó que la nueva plataforma estará disponible durante el trimestre actual.
Según explicó Nadella, el objetivo es que la nueva app de Copilot incluya todas las herramientas de IA de Microsoft, entre ellas el chatbot homónimo, las funciones agénticas y las herramientas de programación.
El CEO de Microsoft remarcó que Copilot está evolucionando rápidamente y que el enfoque está puesto en el trabajo colaborativo y la automatización de tareas. "Este trimestre vamos a integrar todas las experiencias de Copilot, incluyendo la programación, en una súper app. Este es un gran paso adelante, y espero poder compartir más detalles pronto", mencionó.
Una súper app de Copilot estará disponible pronto, confirma Microsoft
Microsoft no es la primera empresa que intenta aglutinar todas sus herramientas de IA bajo una misma aplicación. OpenAI lleva algún tiempo tratando de hacer lo mismo con la app de escritorio de ChatGPT, aunque la experiencia todavía dista bastante de ser la ideal.
El problema que tienen este tipo de aplicaciones es que, si no se hacen de forma correcta, intentan abarcar demasiado y no se destacan en ninguna tarea en particular. Es cierto que reunir varias funciones principales dentro de un mismo software es crucial para combatir la fragmentación excesiva, que es un mal del que Copilot no ha podido escapar. Sin embargo, debe ser una herramienta cohesiva y no un wrapper que reúna múltiples características solo porque son parte de la misma marca.
Todavía no está muy claro cómo planea abordar Microsoft la súper app de Copilot en materia de disponibilidad de modelos. Si bien la relación con OpenAI ya no es buena como en años anteriores, siguen dependiendo parcialmente de sus desarrollos. Pero los de Redmond también están avanzando con firmeza en la creación de modelos de lenguaje propios que tienen un desempeño similar al de sus rivales.
El mes pasado, Microsoft estrenó MAI-Thinking-1, su primer modelo de razonamiento de desarrollo totalmente in-house. Este se ha sumado a otras varias IA de la familia MAI, que recientemente también ha incorporado una versión enfocada en la ciberseguridad: MAI-Cyber-1-Flash.
Una súper app de Copilot podría ser el escenario ideal para que la compañía expanda el acceso a sus modelos de inteligencia artificial propios. Si se cumple con lo que ha prometido Nadella, deberíamos tener novedades en el corto plazo.

articles.title: CRTC suspends deadlines for telecoms to address issues over junk fees
articles.text:
The CRTC is giving major telecoms more time to respond to issues related to their compliance with the prohibition of “junk fees” related to plan switching.
On Wednesday, the regulator posted an update on its website noting that it has suspended the July 30 deadline for Bell, Rogers and Telus to address these issues. The CRTC says it was responded to a request from the Public Interest Advocacy Centre and Telus to delay these proceedings, and it will decide a new deadline once it’s reviewed their case.
This comes after the CRTC banned junk fees in March, which were historically in place to discourage consumers from exploring other plan options due to the costs associated with switching, such as activation fees. Naturally, this was an anti-competitive practice, especially when Canadians already pay some of the highest telecom prices in the world.
The ban took effect in June, but it was quickly discovered that the Big Three were still charging these fees anyway, arguing that they were exempt from the ruling. The CRTC said the carriers could face fines of up to $10 million for violating this ban but gave them a window to inquire further. That was originally until July 30, but now, it remains to be seen how much more time will be granted.
Source: CRTC Via: iPhone in Canada

articles.title: Jahrzehntelang unsichtbar: Software findet Beteigeuzes geheimen Begleitstern
articles.text:
Rätsel am Sternenhimmel: Software liefert Nachweise, die kein Teleskop zeigen kann
Ein Team um den französischen Astronomen Miguel Montargès vom Observatoire de Paris hat die bislang detailreichste Aufnahme des roten Überriesen Beteigeuze und seines neu entdeckten Begleitsterns veröffentlicht. Wie in einem Artikel der Fachzeitschrift Astronomy & Astrophysics (PDF) dokumentiert wird, gelang der Nachweis durch extrem aufwendige Datenverarbeitung.
Monatelang rechneten Algorithmen das blendende Licht des Hauptsterns aus den Aufnahmen heraus. Übrig blieb ein leuchtender Punkt auf den Monitoren. Dieser Punkt ist Beteigeuze B.
Signalverarbeitung am Very Large Telescope
Ausgangspunkt der Analyse waren Beobachtungen mit dem SPHERE-Instrument am Very Large Telescope der Europäischen Südsternwarte ESO im südamerikanischen Chile. Montargès und sein Team nutzten im Dezember 2024 die von der theoretischen Physik vorhergesagte maximale Elongation des Begleiters aus. Dieser astronomische Fachbegriff beschreibt den Zeitpunkt des größten sichtbaren seitlichen Abstands zwischen zwei Himmelskörpern, von der Erde aus betrachtet.
Die Herausforderung bei der Beobachtung gleicht dem Versuch, ein Glühwürmchen zu fotografieren, das direkt neben einem stark leuchtenden Leuchtturm fliegt. Komplexe Algorithmen zur Mustererkennung und Rauschunterdrückung kamen zum Einsatz, um das astronomische Störsignal und die optischen Aberrationen der Erdatmosphäre restlos herauszurechnen. Ein simpler Blick durch Linsen reicht längst nicht.
„Ich bin von meinem Stuhl aufgesprungen, als ich die prozessierten Bilder sah“, zeigte sich Montargès gegenüber der ESO begeistert. Das berichtet Spektrum der Wissenschaft. Beteigeuze B weist den Auswertungen zufolge eine physikalische Masse von etwa 2,6 bis 3,1 Sonnenmassen auf. Er umkreist seinen riesigen Wirtsstern in einem derart geringen Abstand, dass konventionelle Abbildungsverfahren an der reinen Helligkeit des Hauptsterns zwangsläufig scheitern mussten. Der kleine Begleiter gehört in die Kategorie der Hauptreihensterne. Er steht damit am Anfang seines stellaren Lebenszyklus.
Die Vorgeschichte von Siwarha am Gemini North
Die Jagd nach dem unsichtbaren Begleiter nahm im Juli 2025 erstmals konkrete Züge an. Der Forscher Steve B. Howell vom Ames Research Center der US-Weltraumbehörde Nasa nutzte das Gemini-North-Teleskop im US-Bundesstaat Hawaii für interferometrische Aufnahmen. Wie das Jet Propulsion Laboratory mitteilt, fand Howell den Stern exakt an der vorberechneten Position.
Er taufte ihn „Siwarha“. Diese Namensgebung folgt einer klaren historischen Logik. Der Eigenname „Beteigeuze“ leitet sich ursprünglich aus dem Arabischen ab und bedeutet in etwa „die Hand der Riesin“. „Siwarha“ wiederum lässt sich mit „ihr Armreif“ übersetzen. Das ergibt ein schlüssiges Bild. Der kleine Begleiter kreist gewissermaßen als eng anliegendes Schmuckstück um die Sternenhand.
Untermauert wurde die Entdeckung Anfang 2026 durch ultraviolette Spektralanalysen des Hubble-Weltraumteleskops. Die Astrophysikerin Andrea Dupree vom Center for Astrophysics in der US-amerikanischen Stadt Cambridge wies damals eine sich bewegende Bugwelle in der äußeren Atmosphäre des Hauptsterns nach. Dieser verdichtete Gasstrom folgt genau der vermuteten Umlaufbahn des kleinen Begleiters. Der Riesenstern verschluckt seinen winzigen Nachbarn danach phasenweise fast vollständig. Diese Indizienkette war extrem stark.
Das Ende der Supernova-Theorie für 2020
Beteigeuze sorgte in den Jahren 2019 und 2020 für erhebliche Aufregung, als der Stern massiv an Leuchtkraft verlor. Medien spekulierten damals intensiv über eine unmittelbar bevorstehende Supernovaexplosion. Die jüngsten Analysen bestätigen nun, dass ein enormer lokaler Staubauswurf die tatsächliche Ursache für diese historische Verdunkelung war. Der kleine Begleitstern beeinflusst zwar die zirkumstellare Umgebung massiv, löst aber nicht die damaligen enormen Schwankungen der Helligkeit aus. Er erzeugt lediglich physikalische Bugwellen.
Ein Restzweifel bleibt: Die spektakulären Bilder von SPHERE basieren tiefgreifend auf statistischen Wahrscheinlichkeitsmodellen und radikaler Rauschunterdrückung. Die Berechnungen filtern gezielt jene Informationen aus dem Rohmaterial, die in den Augen der Software als störendes Sternenlicht klassifiziert werden. Beobachter:innen müssen blind darauf vertrauen, dass der Algorithmus nicht unabsichtlich Bildartefakte als Himmelskörper interpretiert. Physikalisch eindeutig bewiesen ist die gravitative Bindung von Beteigeuze B an den Hauptstern erst dann, wenn er auf der exakt gegenüberliegenden Seite seiner Umlaufbahn fotografiert werden kann. Das wird voraussichtlich im Jahr 2027 geschehen.
Bis dahin liefert die aktuelle Beobachtungskampagne ein eindrucksvolles Zeugnis davon, wie stark Software die physikalischen Grenzen moderner Optik erweitert. Die reine Hardwareleistung der Großteleskope rückt zunehmend in den Hintergrund.
Dass der Stern bei uns heute überhaupt Beteigeuze und im englischen Sprachraum Betelgeuse heißt, beruht übrigens auf kuriosen historischen Übersetzungsfehlern, an denen der Name „Siwarha“ nun elegant vorbeigreift. Ursprung beider Begriffe ist das arabische Yad al-Jauzāʾ. Mittelalterliche Übersetzer verwechselten den ersten Buchstaben, wodurch versehentlich aus einem Y ein B wurde. Englische und französische Astronomen übernahmen diesen Irrtum unkorrigiert. Der deutsche Name verdankt seine abweichende Schreibweise einem weiteren profanen Lesefehler. In der historischen Frakturschrift sahen sich das kleine l und das kleine i zum Verwechseln ähnlich. Beim Übertragen der internationalen Kataloge wurde aus Betelgeuse schlicht Beteigeuze. Wir nennen den Himmelskörper bis heute so.

articles.title: Memory maker SK hynix's profit rises 557% amid global shortage, expansion costs climb to $27 billion — shares slide despite mammoth earnings as expectations outpace reality and global AI selloffs continue
articles.text:
Memory maker SK hynix's profit rises 557% amid global shortage, expansion costs climb to $27 billion — shares slide despite mammoth earnings as expectations outpace reality and global AI selloffs continue
Q3 DRAM bit shipments are guided up around 10%, one quarter after average selling prices climbed roughly 30%.
SK hynix reported second-quarter revenue of 79.32 trillion won and operating profit of 60.54 trillion won on Wednesday, the latter up 557% year over year at a record 76% operating margin, and used the same Seoul earnings call to lift its 2026 capital spending guidance to the high 40 trillion won range as AI server demand keeps outrunning what the company can produce. Third-quarter DRAM bit shipments are guided up around 10% sequentially, following a quarter in which DRAM average selling prices rose roughly 30%, and NAND prices rose in the mid-50% range.
SK priced 177.9 million American depositary receipts at $149 each earlier this month, raising $26.51 billion in the largest share sale by a non-U.S. company on record, with the SEC filing earmarking proceeds for Korean manufacturing facilities and equipment, including EUV scanners.
Wednesday's capex number is roughly the same size and funds an accelerated mass production schedule at the M15X fab in Cheongju, the Yongin Phase 1 cleanroom that opens in early 2027, and the previously announced P&T7 advanced packaging plant and M17 NAND base, which SK hynix said will be built in phases according to customer demand. Cash and short-term investments hit 88 trillion won at the quarter's end, up 33.6 trillion won in three months, against interest-bearing debt of 18.6 trillion won and a debt-to-equity ratio of 7%.
CEO Kwak Noh-jung called 2027 the worst year of the shortage on the day of the Nasdaq listing and put the end of the crunch beyond 2030. Full-year DRAM demand is growing at a mid-20% rate by the company's own estimate, against bit shipments guided up around 10% next quarter. None of the capacity now being funded will produce wafers before 2027.
Operating profit landed below the 64.1 trillion won that brokerages surveyed by Yonhap Infomax had modeled. Executives attributed the softer blended DRAM ASP to product mix and to high-value shipments pushed into the second half, and said the gap should close as HBM4 and 1c-node conventional DRAM ramp up. HBM4 entered mass production during the quarter, and HBM4E samples have shipped, with volume production targeted for 2027.
Triggered by global selloffs, SK hynix closed down around 10% in Seoul on Wednesday, and Samsung Electronics fell 5%, with the KOSPI ending the session 6% lower and below 6,000 for the first time since April 14. The index touched 5,262 at one point, down almost 13%, taking its five-session decline to 17% and cutting a year-to-date gain that had reached 116% in June to 34%. Over the past month, SK hynix has lost 47% of its value and Samsung 37%. The KOSPI fell 10.84% on Tuesday and triggered a marketwide circuit breaker after SK hynix's American depositary receipts dropped below the $149 price at which they listed on Nasdaq on July 10.
Weaker shareholder-return expectations compounded the earnings miss, with SK hynix telling analysts only that additional returns remain under evaluation and would be disclosed within the year. Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, told Bloomberg that "expectations had simply moved ahead of what even another record quarter could deliver."
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
CXMT closed its Shanghai debut up 466% on Monday after raising 57.92 billion yuan for DRAM wafer lines, and a report last week put China at low-volume production of domestic immersion DUV scanners running to around five units this year. TrendForce still has conventional DRAM contract prices rising 13% to 18% in the third quarter, with NAND up 10% to 15%.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Luke James is a freelance writer and journalist. Although his background is in legal, he has a personal interest in all things tech, especially hardware and microelectronics, and anything regulatory.
